Innate immunity is present at birth and provides protection against a wide range of foreign substances, including many microorganisms that cause infectious diseases.  Acquired immunity refers to the ability of the body to respond to specific foreign substances, leading to the production of new antibodies that are able to recognise and bind to those specific foreign substances.
